newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern, other railroads gain.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern, other railroads gain.

text.p: Railroad shares attracted heavy investing Tuesday on speculation some carriers may mimic CSX Inc and Conrail Inc, two industry giants which unveiled an $8.4 billion merger this morning.
Anthony Hatch, NatWest Securities railroad analyst, said, "There is a sense of deal-mania in the group. There are a lot of arbitrageurs getting into the stocks saying 'Who's next?'"
In afternoon NYSE trade, Conrail stock was up 14-1/4 to 85-1/4. The stock and cash deal valued Conrail at $92.50 per share before CSX shares declined three to 46-1/2."

Explaining the sharp rise in Norfolk Southern Corp shares, he said investors are realizing Norfolk could benefit significantly from a CSX/Conrail merger because federal regulators would likely force the new company into giving Norfolk trackage rights as a deal approval condition.
Norfolk shares were up 3-1/4 to an all-time high 95-1/4.
"When Union Pacific (Corp ) merged with Southern Pacific, they got approval by giving Burlington Northern (Santa Fe Corp ) competitive access and trackage rights," he said.
"So Norfolk Southern, as the odd man out, may get access to these markets (those served by a combined Conrail/CSX) for free," he said.

In a statement issued after merger was announced, Norfolk said it "recognizes that the proposed merger of Conrail and CSX, if consummated, would have very significant implications for the nation's transportation system and for the shipping public. This combination raises serious concerns."
It added that "whatever happens in this process initiated by our competitor, Norfolk Southern will be a part of it. We do not rule out any options."
Meanwhile, Union Pacific Corp shares edged up 3/8 to 73-3/4, MK Rail Corp added 5/8 to 7-1/4, Delaware Otsego Corp rose 3/4 to 8-1/4 and RailTex Inc improved by 1/2 to 20-1/2.
